questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: The famous 21 cm radio astronomy line of neutral atomic hydrogen ($1s$) arises from:
optionsEn: Hyperfine splitting between parallel ($F = 1$) and antiparallel ($F = 0$) electron and proton spins
questions.explanationEn: The interaction between the electron spin ($S = 1/2$) and proton nuclear spin ($I = 1/2$) splits the $1s$ ground state into $F = 1$ and $F = 0$, separated by $\Delta\nu \approx 1420\text{ MHz}$ ($\lambda \approx 21\text{ cm}$).

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: In Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR), the Larmor resonance frequency $\omega_0$ of a nucleus with gyromagnetic ratio $\gamma_N$ in a static field $B_0$ is:
questions.explanationEn: Magnetic resonance occurs when the RF frequency matches the Larmor precession frequency $\omega_0 = \gamma_N B_0$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: In pure rotational Raman spectroscopy of a linear diatomic molecule, the rotational selection rule is:
questions.explanationEn: Raman scattering is a two-photon process (each photon carries angular momentum 1), yielding $\Delta J = 0$ (Rayleigh), $+2$ (Stokes S-branch), and $-2$ (anti-Stokes O-branch).

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: The Mössbauer effect relies on:
optionsEn: Laser cooling of free gas atoms
Recoilless emission and resonant absorption of gamma rays by nuclei bound in a solid crystal lattice
questions.explanationEn: When a nucleus is tightly bound in a crystal, recoil momentum is taken up by the macroscopic lattice mass, making recoil energy negligible and enabling ultra-narrow resonant gamma absorption.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: The spin-orbit interaction Hamiltonian $H_{\text{SO}} \propto \frac{1}{r}\frac{dV}{dr}\,\mathbf{L} \cdot \mathbf{S}$ in a hydrogen-like ion of nuclear charge $Z$ produces fine-structure energy splitting scaling with $Z$ as:
questions.explanationEn: Since $V \propto Z/r$ and $\langle 1/r^3 \rangle \propto Z^3$, the spin-orbit splitting scales as $Z \cdot Z^3 = Z^4$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about vibrational spectra of anharmonic diatomic molecules (Morse potential) are TRUE?
optionsEn: Energy levels get closer together as vibrational quantum number $v$ increases
Overtone transitions ($\Delta v = \pm 2, \pm 3, \dots$) become weakly allowed in addition to the fundamental $\Delta v = \pm 1$
The dissociation energy from the ground state is $D_0 = D_e - E_0$, where $E_0$ is the zero-point energy
The molecule has infinitely many bound vibrational states
questions.explanationEn: A, B, and C are exact Morse-potential properties. A Morse potential has finite depth $D_e$ and supports only a finite number of bound vibrational levels (D is false).

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: What is the total number of microstates for two equivalent $p$-electrons ($p^2$ configuration)?
questions.explanationEn: A $p$-subshell has 6 spin-orbitals, so $\binom{6}{2} = 15$ microstates (corresponding to $^1 S_0 [1] + ^3 P_{0,1,2} [9] + ^1 D_2 [5] = 15$).

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: What is the degeneracy of the rotational level $J = 4$ of a linear rigid diatomic molecule (ignoring nuclear spin)?
questions.explanationEn: Rotational degeneracy is $2J + 1 = 2(4) + 1 = 9$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: For a hydrogen atom in its $n = 1$ ground state with proton spin $I = 1/2$ and electron $J = 1/2$, how many total hyperfine magnetic sublevels ($M_F$ states) exist across both $F = 0$ and $F = 1$?
questions.explanationEn: Total states = $(2I + 1)(2J + 1) = 2 \times 2 = 4$ (1 state in $F = 0$ and 3 states in $F = 1$).

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn:
For the $K_\alpha$ X-ray line of copper ($Z = 29$) vs. aluminum ($Z = 13$), using Moseley's law $
u \propto (Z - 1)^2$, what is the ratio of their $K_\alpha$ frequencies $
u_{	ext{Cu}} / 
u_{	ext{Al}}$? (Round to 2 decimal places.)
questions.explanationEn: $\frac{\nu_{\text{Cu}}}{\nu_{\text{Al}}} = \left(\frac{29 - 1}{13 - 1}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{28}{12}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{7}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{49}{9} \approx 5.44$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: For a 2-level atomic system in a cavity at $T = 300\text{ K}$ ($k_B T \approx 0.026\text{ eV}$), for an optical transition of photon energy $h\nu = 2.0\text{ eV}$, which emission process overwhelmingly dominates in thermal equilibrium?
questions.explanationEn: Since $h\nu / (k_B T) \approx 77 \gg 1$, $\frac{R_{\text{stim}}}{R_{\text{spon}}} = \frac{1}{e^{77} - 1} \approx 10^{-34}$, so spontaneous emission overwhelmingly dominates at optical frequencies in thermal equilibrium.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: When a proton (nuclear spin $I = 1/2$) is placed in a magnetic field $B_0$ in an NMR spectrometer, the chemical shift $\delta$ (in ppm) arises from:
optionsEn: Diamagnetic shielding of the external field $B_0$ by surrounding local valence electrons
questions.explanationEn: Induced orbital currents in the surrounding electron cloud create a small opposing local field $-\sigma B_0$, shifting the effective field to $B_{\text{eff}} = B_0(1 - \sigma)$ and revealing chemical environments.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: By the Landé interval rule for $LS$-coupled spin-orbit multiplets ($H_{\text{SO}} = A \mathbf{L} \cdot \mathbf{S}$), what is the ratio of energy splittings $\frac{E(^3 D_3) - E(^3 D_2)}{E(^3 D_2) - E(^3 D_1)}$?
questions.explanationEn: The Landé interval rule states $E(J) - E(J - 1) = A J$. Thus $[E(3) - E(2)] / [E(2) - E(1)] = 3 / 2$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about spectroscopic term symbols for equivalent $p^2$ electrons are TRUE?
optionsEn: $^3 S$, $^1 P$, and $^3 D$ are forbidden for $p^2$
The sum of $(2S+1)(2L+1)$ over all allowed terms equals 15
According to Hund's rules, $^1 D_2$ is the ground state of $p^2$
Only $^1 S$, $^3 P$, and $^1 D$ terms are allowed by the Pauli exclusion principle
questions.explanationEn: A, B, and C are exact ($1 + 9 + 5 = 15$). By Hund's rules, maximum spin $^3 P_0$ is the ground state, not $^1 D_2$ (D is false).

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: In the Stern-Gerlach experiment with an atom in a $^2 P_{3/2}$ state, into how many discrete beams does the atomic beam split when passing through an inhomogeneous magnetic field?
questions.explanationEn: Number of split beams equals $2J + 1 = 2(3/2) + 1 = 4$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: A laser cavity of length $L = 50\text{ cm}$ has mirror reflectivities $R_1 = 1.0$ and $R_2 = e^{-0.2} \approx 0.8187$. Ignoring internal losses, what is the threshold gain coefficient $\gamma_{\text{th}}$ (in $\text{m}^{-1}$)?
questions.explanationEn: $R_1 R_2 e^{2\gamma_{\text{th}} L} = 1 \implies e^{-0.2} e^{2\gamma_{\text{th}}(0.5)} = 1 \implies \gamma_{\text{th}} = 0.2\text{ m}^{-1}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: What is the total number of microstates in a $d^3$ electronic configuration?
questions.explanationEn: A $d$-subshell has 10 spin-orbitals, so $\binom{10}{3} = \frac{10 \times 9 \times 8}{6} = 120$ microstates.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: In a hydrogenic ion, the Lyman-alpha ($n = 2 \to 1$) photon energy is $10.2\text{ eV}$ for $Z = 1$. What is the Lyman-alpha photon energy (in eV) for doubly ionized lithium $\text{Li}^{2+}$ ($Z = 3$)?
questions.explanationEn: Transition energies scale as $Z^2$: $10.2 \times 3^2 = 10.2 \times 9 = 91.8\text{ eV}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 1)
questions.questionTextEn: In a Mössbauer experiment using $^{57}\text{Fe}$ ($E_\gamma = 14.4\text{ keV}$), the source is moved at speed $v = 3\text{ mm/s}$ toward the absorber. Taking $c = 3 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}$, what is the Doppler energy shift $\Delta E = E_\gamma (v/c)$ in nano-electronvolts (neV)?
questions.explanationEn: $\Delta E = (14.4 \times 10^3\text{ eV}) \times \frac{3 \times 10^{-3}}{3 \times 10^8} = 14.4 \times 10^3 \times 10^{-11} = 1.44 \times 10^{-7}\text{ eV} = 144\text{ neV}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE PH Topic • Atomic and Molecular Physics (Set 1)
